correctness.rationale: After translation to the common solution, a sampled reflection acts on z∈C as exp(2ijθ) times conjugation. The alternating sum S has generating polynomial 2^(−r) z^(−floor(r/2))(1+z)^r, so every listed index occurs with the stated binomial weight. For even r, the average is complex multiplication by exp(iSθ)cos(Sθ), either invertible or zero; independence gives the claimed geometric time. For odd r, the average is rank-one projection to L_(Sθ). A nonzero projected vector survives exactly when the next axis is not perpendicular. The support differences realize every integer from −r to r. A perpendicular ordered pair, when available, occurs almost surely by independent disjoint two-block trials; without one there is no killing after a surviving first projection. Even an exceptional nonzero start has strictly positive survival probability at its first projection because both distinct axes L_0 and L_θ occur. Thus the iff is valid for each fixed nonzero start; only the stated odd waiting-time formula assumes a generic first projection. The least positive d with cos(dθ)=0 is b/2 for a reduced even denominator b, and otherwise none exists; together with the even support and odd difference support this yields both thresholds. The killed transition probabilities give p^T Q^(k−1)1; uniform pair-trial decay implies spectral radius less than one and justifies summing the inverse series. Bounded independent rational calculation reproduced 61/9, 36, and 8 blocks for the stated examples; the general claim rests on the proof, not the uploaded checker.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Exact absorption requires deriving the alternating binomial support, separating rotations from projections, proving the necessity for exceptional starts, and counting the allowed support differences. originality.rationale: The algorithm itself and its convergence theory are prior work. The inspected statements do not resolve exact hitting under fresh reflection bundles: neither the even/odd denominator thresholds for this process nor the killed-chain first-solution law are covered. Deterministic planar DR and stochastic planar Kaczmarz have material connections but different transition processes. This is a scoped, best-of-knowledge finding.
residual_risks: Focused literature and ranked index retrieval are not exhaustive; an equivalent result in stochastic projection products might be indexed differently.
The comparison to the indexed regular-frame result is based on its actual finding; its remaining discussion was not retrieved.

value.rationale: The two-normal geometry is the minimal nontrivial instance of the published randomized method. The exact-hitting boundary separates almost-sure finite absorption from indefinite nonzero trajectories even when general convergence estimates apply. The sharp parity thresholds explain which reflection counts can possibly work; the waiting laws quantify the block and reflection costs, beyond merely identifying resonant examples. The value is for the exact-arithmetic stochastic scheme, not a finite-precision performance assertion.
